newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KEY ELEMENTS OF WEDNESDAY'S EUROPEAN CUP MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KEY ELEMENTS OF WEDNESDAY'S EUROPEAN CUP MATCHES.

text.p: Analysis of key elements in Wednesday's European Cup quarter-final first leg matches:

Ajax, last season's beaten finalists, have had a miserable first half of the season and injuries before the winter break and a change in personnel have left Ajax flat, although the recent win against arch-rivals Feyenoord hinted at a return to form.

Ajax have no-one suspended for Wednesday's match but five players, including Patrick Kluivert have picked up one yellow card. But Ajax will be without Winston Bogarde, dropped from the squad after refusing to accept a substitute's place on the bench.
Atletico Madrid will start their biggest game of the season without suspended striker Kiko, whose run of good form has helped to turn round the season for the Spanish champions.

Kiko's place up-front will be taken by Leonardo Biaginni, who will partner fellow Argentine Juan Eduardo Esnaider. Atletico have been boosted by the news that playmaker Jose Luis Caminero has recovered from a stomach bug but there is a doubt over defender Toni Munoz, who picked up a knock on Saturday.
Dortmund's European player of the year Matthias Sammer has been ruled out because of a calf injury he picked up playing for Germany in last week's friendly with Israel.
Wolfgang Feiersinger is standing by to deputise for Sammer as he did in Saturday's 4-1 Bundesliga win over 1860 Munich.

Portuguese international Paulo Sousa took no part in training on Monday because of an upset stomach but Dortmund coach Ottmar Hitzfeld is confident the midfielder, who scored a spectacular goal against 1860 and was generally oustanding, will be fit for Wednesday.

Auxerre were knocked out of the French Cup by second division Troyes on Friday and have gone four games without a goal. Midfield playmakers Moussa Saib and Sabri Lamouchi have collectively lost form and will need to improve rapidly to get anything from Wednesday. - - -

Manchester United boss Alex Ferguson was named England's manager of the month on Monday which came as no surprise as his team have surged four points clear in the title race. United will be without the injured Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt but Roy Keane is expected to recover from the ankle injury that forced him out of Saturday's League match with Coventry.

In contrast to United, Porto's form has recently slumped and they may be without Brazilian forward Jardel who damaged his wrist when he ran into a crash barrier after Friday's league match against Amadora. Porto lost for the first time this season last weekend and face a United side playing some of their best football of the season. None of their players are suspended but 10 are on a yellow card.

Rosenborg have just returned from 12 days on the Mediterranean island of Cyprus, where they won two matches and drew one in an unofficial Scandinavian cup competition. The have no injured or suspended players, but have several -- Jon Olav Hjelde, Roar Strand, Bent Skammelsrud, Harald Brattbakk, Bjoern Otto Bragstad and Trond Egil Soltvedt -- on a yellow card.

Juventus had Alessandro del Piero, Didider Deschamps and Alen Boksic missing with injuries in their 2-0 win over Vicenza in Serie A on Saturday. Deschamps should be fit for Wednesday's match, but Del Piero is definitely out and Boksic unlikely to even make the trip.
